title: {Syn} Elliptic Curves Add Points Like Numbers
content:
An elliptic curve is not an ellipse; it is usually an equation like y^2 = x^3 + ax + b. Its rational points can be added with a geometric chord-and-tangent rule.

That group structure powers elliptic-curve cryptography and also sits at the heart of deep arithmetic questions, including the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture.

Why it matters: number theory keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
